item.title: Pregnant, not sidelined
item.dc:creator: Théa Spoorenberg
item.description:
The Link · Théa Spoorenberg · Oct 27 · 9:00 a.m.
For decades, pregnancy was treated as a career risk for female athletes. Contracts lapsed, sponsors disappeared, and rankings evaporated. That is changing, with the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) committing to paying competitors 12 months of maternity leave and Athletics Canada no longer classifying pregnancy as an "injury."

item.title: Ottawa monument dedicated to LGBT Purge survivors now open
item.dc:creator: James Bossinakis
item.description:
The Link · James Bossinakis · Oct 27 · 9:00 a.m.
The National Monument, called "Thunderhead," was erected in Ottawa to memorialize those affected by Canada's LGBT Purge. It recently had its grand opening, led by purge survivors, community leaders and Indigenous partners. The funding for this monument was given to the LGBT Purge Fund as part of a $145 million settlement after a class action lawsuit by 2SLGBTQI+ service members.

item.title: Decline in Canadian acceptance of gender diversity
item.dc:creator: Marissa Guthrie
item.description:
The Link · Marissa Guthrie · Oct 27 · 9:00 a.m.
A study by Statistics Canada demonstrated that although Canadians have largely held more progressive attitudes regarding gender-based violence, fewer participants in 2025 than in 2018 agreed that individuals should be able to express their identity however they want. In 2018, 85 per cent agreed with this, compared with 77 per cent in 2025.

item.title: Une récolte record de bleuets sauvages dans la région
item.dc:creator: Étienne Harvey-Soucy
item.description:
La Pige · Étienne Harvey-Soucy · 26 oct. · 14 h 50
L’industrie du bleuet a connu une saison exceptionnelle au Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean et en Haute-Mauricie. Pour 2026, la récolte est estimée à 114 millions de livres, dépassant le précédent record régional de 106 millions, établi en 2005. Cette hausse s’explique notamment par l’agrandissement des bleuetières et les conditions météorologiques généralement favorables.

item.title: Celebrating CAEO Québec’s 50th Anniversary
item.dc:creator: Mara Gibea and Justin Friedberg
item.description:
The McGill Daily · Mara Gibea and Justin Friedberg · Oct 26 · 8:00 a.m.
The Daily spoke with Kimberly Wong, current director general of SILK, and Gregg Blachford, former president of Gay Line (1993-1996) and director of McGill’s Career and Placement Service (CaPS), about CAEO Québec and the SILK program. We discussed queer education and services for English-speaking schools, volunteering and outreach, allyship, and counteracting shame with queer joy.

item.title: Queer Language is Queer Resistance
item.dc:creator: The editorial team
item.description:
The McGill Daily · The editorial team · Oct 26 · 8:00 a.m.
In late 2025, Quebec banned the use of gender-inclusive language in all government communications written in French. With the recent election of Paul St-Pierre Plamondon of the minority Parti Québécois (PQ) who has supported this exclusionary measure, it is now more important than ever to be conscious of how language serves LGBTQ+ communities.

item.dc:creator: Élodie Bréniel, Élise Lécaudé et Juliette Fournier
item.description:
Montréal Campus · Élodie Bréniel, Élise Lécaudé et Juliette Fournier · 25 oct. · 17 h 00
En novembre 2024, une étudiante déclare à la police de la prestigieuse université Cornell qu’elle a été agressée par des membres d’une fraternité. Le corps étudiant est outré : certains lancent des œufs sur la maison de Chi Phi. L’Université, quant à elle, met en place un groupe de travail pour bonifier la sensibilisation aux violences sexuelles.
